title: TWINE
knowledge: For KMC GCC 2.7.2, use unsigned C division when the MIPS target uses an unsigned multiply-high sequence. For division by 10, a u32 numerator can produce multu with 0xCCCCCCCD followed by mfhi and a logical shift by 3. A signed numerator selects a different constant and sign correction.
For gcc-2.7.2-kmc float comparisons, writing `right > left` instead of `left < right` can reverse the order of the two operand loads while preserving the same c.lt.s instruction and NaN behavior.

KMC GCC can fold a signed-byte conversion into lb. If the target instead reads with lbu and explicitly sign-extends with sll/sra by 24, try a volatile u8 load followed by the signed-byte cast. Preserve any subsequent u16 narrowing only where the target uses it.

With KMC GCC, try typed struct members in place of byte-offset access macros when access widths and control flow already agree but aliasing, load order, or register allocation differ. Preserve the observed field offsets and access widths.
When a shared result local adds a move into the return register, try returning directly from each path. Compare the target's branch order and return delay slot after the rewrite.

When KMC GCC turns consecutive float zero stores into integer sw $zero but the target uses FPU stores, try initializing a register f32 local to 0.0f and using it across the stores. Compare mtc1/swc1 and the stack layout.
For gcc-2.7.2-kmc, a 16-byte struct assignment can produce a four-word load followed by four-word store sequence; use a value struct copy when the target groups the loads and stores.

Under GCC 2.7.2 KMC, calls through an unprototyped function declaration apply default argument promotions: an f32 actual becomes double, changing MIPS FP argument setup and stack frame. Add an accurate f32 parameter prototype when the target passes a single-precision value.

Under TWINE's gcc-2.7.2-kmc -mgp32 -mfp32 profile, scalar float function parameters can arrive in integer argument registers and be moved into an FPU register by the callee. Keep the C parameter as float when the target begins with `mtc1 $a1,$fs0`; passing an integer or changing the callee prototype changes call setup.

When adjacent structure stores differ only in order, try reordering the independent source assignments; GCC's loop optimization may also change register allocation depending on the surrounding assignment order.
For unsigned division of a signed halfword, cast the sign-extended s16 value to u32 before dividing; casting the load to u16 instead changes the generated division sequence.

For KMC GCC 2.7.2, a direct float- or double-to-u32 cast can produce the target's 2^31 comparison, adjustment, truncation, and high-bit OR. Start with a u32 assignment or cast and keep the original input precision. Check any following clamp against the resulting paths.

On gcc-2.7.2-kmc, use one local per repeated floating-point scale when the target keeps each literal in a callee-saved FPR across calls. Update an address-taken stack vector directly with compound assignments when the target reloads each element before adding.

For a TWINE float wrapper that calls a double-precision helper, explicitly cast the f32 input to f64 for the call and cast the result back to f32; gcc-2.7.2-kmc places cvt.d.s in the jal delay slot and emits cvt.s.d after return.

When GCC 2.7.2 KMC combines two short-circuit zero tests into sltiu/sltiu/or but the target uses consecutive branches to a common failure block, spell out the control flow with gotos: branch to cleanup on a zero first value, branch to success on a nonzero second value, and place cleanup before success with a jump over success.

When assembly supplies an offset in bytes, form the address from a byte-sized symbol or convert the base to a byte pointer before adding the offset. This applies to pointers loaded from a field too. With an s32 pointer, C scales every added index by four. Preserve the actual access width separately.

When a global command-buffer pointer is advanced after each emitted word, declare the pointer object itself volatile (for example, `extern void * volatile gdl_head`). A plain pointer declaration lets GCC collapse successive assignments into only the final pointer update.

When a three-word value is copied through output fields that the target loads and stores as floats (lwc1/swc1), type the source and destination elements as f32 rather than copying them through integer words; MIPS GCC then emits the FPU transfers and can substantially improve matching.

When gcc-2.7.2-kmc puts a field store in a conditional branch delay slot and the condition reads a global, explicitly cache the global before the store, then test the cached local. With the global read after the store in C, GCC can leave the store before the branch and emit a nop.

For byte-offset access to a table of 32-bit fields, keep the element load as a 32-bit dereference but form the address through an s8 pointer, e.g. `*((s32 *)((s8 *)&base + byte_offset))`. This preserves byte addressing without changing lw/lbu semantics.

When a lookup table contains float values consumed by floating-point arithmetic, load it through f32 pointers rather than s32 pointers; the integer form inserts numeric conversions instead of loading float bit patterns.

For KMC GCC, declare byte tables or buffers as u8 elements when the target uses lbu and observes the zero-extended value. Signed char or s8 can select lb and change later sign extension or register use.

If a call forwards incoming arguments unchanged, check the callee prototype and pass those arguments explicitly in C. This includes a forwarded first argument before an output pointer, unchanged middle register arguments, and any later stack arguments. Omitting unchanged arguments can shift the remaining ones.

When a loop's invariant field load and cached global count are scheduled in the wrong order relative to an index initialization, explicitly load both into locals before initializing the index and use the cached count in the loop condition.

For GCC 2.7.2 KMC, when a shared early return belongs between a null check and a copy, explicitly branch to the return label from the first guard and branch over the return to the copy on the non-null path. Returning directly at that label can avoid an extra result-register move.

For GCC 2.7.2 KMC, signed 16-bit locals used as boolean flags can cause register-to-register moves before branch tests, filling delay slots where int locals branch directly and unsigned byte locals emit masking instructions.

When KMC GCC's target groups three integer loads before three stores, try a three-word struct assignment with the actual field types. This can preserve an addressable stack copy before editing a float member or emit distinct field relocations for a global record. Compare register lifetimes and check for floating-point transfers.

KMC GCC 2.7.2 can reserve stack space for an unused local aggregate, including a volatile one, without adding loads or stores. Try a correctly sized local as a diagnostic when frame and saved-register offsets differ uniformly but live stack accesses agree. For an eight-byte gap, examples used a two-word array or a volatile 64-bit local.

When a computed floating-point value is both stored and scaled for a second store, stage the scaled result in a local before either store to encourage the compiler to retain separate FP registers and schedule the multiplication earlier.

With KMC GCC 2.7.2 on MIPS32, if typed pointer arithmetic reverses the target addu operands, add the base and already byte-scaled offset as 32-bit integers in target order and cast back to the pointer type. Test the offset-first form when appropriate and compare both operand order and register allocation.

When the target reloads a pointer field immediately before a store but GCC reuses a previously loaded value, a volatile-qualified pointer-field read at that use can recover the reload. Confirm the target's repeated load and aliasing before applying it.

For GCC 2.7.2 KMC, indexing an array of records can produce a %hi(symbol) plus scaled index followed by a load or store using %lo(symbol); manually adding the scaled offset to a scalar symbol may instead materialize the full address first.

When a default switch-like path sets an index to zero before a shared scaling operation, routing zero through the same scaling expression as the other cases can place the shift in the default jump delay slot under GCC 2.7.2 KMC.

For KMC GCC 2.7.2 at -O1, try expressing a byte stride as an odd factor multiplied first, then a power-of-two factor, when the target's final scaling instruction is a shift. A single literal stride can expand into a differently ordered shift/add sequence.

For KMC GCC 2.7.2 -O2, wrapping an initial scalar load in a do { ... } while (0) can change loop/control-flow lowering and register allocation in string-copy style code; test a narrow scoped block when the target's first byte-copy path has the right operations but later loop branches/registers differ.

For KMC GCC 2.7.2 matrix math, explicitly writing each scalar product and matrix output expression in the target's evaluation sequence can preserve instruction scheduling and reduce register-only mismatches versus precomputing/reordering grouped outputs.
For KMC GCC 2.7.2, explicitly expressing an indexed float address as integer offset plus base can reverse the operands of the generated MIPS addu compared with ordinary pointer indexing.

When the target reads three consecutive unaligned 32-bit words from a global byte table and copies them to a local stack buffer, model the source global as a three-u32 struct rather than u8[]: GCC 2.7.2 KMC can emit lwl/lwr pairs plus swl/swr copies matching the target.

For KMC GCC 2.7.2, assigning three consecutive words through a typed three-word struct can force integer lw/sw copies where equivalent float field assignments use lwc1/swc1. This can recover raw word copies when the target first copies a float vector to stack before modifying one float member; further local layout tuning may still be needed.
At KMC GCC 2.7.2 -O2, expressing an index stride as an odd factor followed by a left shift can alter register allocation even when the arithmetic instruction sequence is equivalent.

When a global address is used as a byte base plus an integer byte offset, cast the base to u8 * before addition (for example `(u8 *)&global_base + byte_offset`) to avoid MIPS GCC scaling the offset by the base pointee size. For 0xFF sentinels at byte fields, use u8 field types when the target forms a 255 immediate; s8 may produce the signed -1 form.

Some TWINE functions are IDO-compiled, not KMC GCC: tell-tales are callee-saved registers stored at low sp offsets (0x18..) with locals above them, and register moves emitted as `or rd, rs, $zero`. When GCC attempts get a wrong frame layout (saves at top), run compiler_experiments/try_compiler with ido-7.1 (flags -O2 -mips2 -G 0 -non_shared -Xcpluscomm -Wab,-r4300_mul -woff 649,838,712) and write clean C (no volatile pads, a plain local array sized to the frame).

In KMC GCC 2.7.2, a typed assignment of a 36-byte struct with word alignment can reproduce the compiler's 16-byte-step block copy loop for 32 bytes followed by a final word copy. Writing the same loop by hand can introduce extra address induction variables and offset differences.

For a switch whose cases select different constants before a common call, repeating the call in each case can let KMC GCC 2.7.2 merge the call while avoiding extra jumps generated by explicit shared goto labels.

For TWINE's KMC GCC 2.7.2, using an explicit pointer local initialized to a global's address and dereferencing it on both sides of a call can produce a saved-register address with repeated offset-zero loads. This works for byte and word loads.

KMC GCC 2.7.2: a 'switch' with only a few sparse cases (e.g. 7 and 14) becomes compare/branch, not a jump table. To get the target's `sltiu/lw jtbl/jr` dispatch, list all intermediate values as explicit empty cases (case 0..6: break; case 8..13: break; case 7: case 14: body). Also, when a callee's bool result is tested with `sll $v0,$v0,24; beqz`, declare it returning s8 and test `(call(...) << 24) != 0` (an `& 0xFF` gives andi instead).

For KMC GCC 2.7.2, test -fno-cse-skip-blocks when repeated branch-separated calls in the target independently materialize the same static format string address but the candidate hoists it to a saved register. This can also recover surrounding register allocation.

For KMC GCC 2.7.2, when a boolean-like integer is held in an argument register but the target copies it to v0 before a final branch, testing a signed 16-bit cast of the value can induce the copy without extra truncation instructions.

For KMC GCC 2.7.2, reorder operands and grouping in a commutative bitwise OR expression when the target computes packed fields in a different order; equivalent grouping can control instruction scheduling.

For KMC GCC 2.7.2, when a 12-byte copy uses three word loads before any store, express it as assignment of a word-aligned three-field struct. Three scalar assignments can produce interleaved loads and stores and change surrounding register allocation.

On KMC GCC 2.7.2, test -fno-strength-reduce when the target keeps independent byte-offset induction variables and rebuilds global-plus-offset addresses inside the loop, but the candidate builds extra pointer cursors and spills registers. Test -fno-schedule-insns separately if target instruction order still differs.

For KMC GCC 2.7.2, three contiguous f32 components may be copied through integer lw/sw when the C uses a three-float struct assignment. This also applies to a byte-indexed destination in a global array.

In KMC GCC 2.7.2, when several switch arms set different call arguments but the target has one shared jal, try spelling out a full call in each arm. GCC can merge the call tails after lowering the arguments, avoiding the extra spills from assigning all arguments to common locals and jumping to a single C call site.

In KMC GCC 2.7.2, when assembly loads a global address once into a saved register and reloads its value through that register across calls, try an explicit local pointer to volatile data. This can preserve the shared address while emitting each load.

For TWINE m2c drafts, verify the literal offset of signed byte loads before keeping a narrowing cast of a loaded word. On big-endian MIPS `(s8)*(s32 *)(base + offset)` can compile to `lb offset+3(base)`. If the target has `lb offset(base)`, express the byte load directly, even when a different path reads a word at that same offset.

Audit m2c expressions `&scalar + offset` when the assembly adds a byte offset to a symbol address. Cast the base to a byte pointer before adding the offset, then dereference with the width shown by the target load or store. Scalar pointer arithmetic scales the offset again.
